articles.title: Cracks in the AI Thesis Part 3
articles.summary: Ramp's October AI Index reports that just 1% of firms in its data account for 80% of spending on OpenAI and Anthropic. That makes revenue unusually dependent on a small group of heavy users. Their September spending per employee was 3.1% below July's peak, even as overall token volumes rose. The index proposes falling model prices as the main explanation. If your AI revenue depends on usage, track what share comes from your largest accounts and whether their spending is recovering before forecasting revenue from token growth.

articles.title: Price War in the Chip Aisle
articles.summary: Five frontier AI models score within five points of each other on an intelligence benchmark, but the cost of running their tasks varies by 3.8 times. Google's Argon is cheapest at $1.99 per task. The comparison includes billed reasoning tokens and tests every model at maximum reasoning effort, so a similar score can come with a very different bill. Before choosing a default model, run the same sample of your application's requests through the candidates at the settings you plan to use and compare the cost of acceptable answers.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Investors Put $6.8B To Work In The Third Quarter, Mostly In Larger Rounds
articles.summary: Cybersecurity startups attracted $6.8 billion in Q3 2026, marking a 50% increase from the previous quarter, driven predominantly by larger funding rounds. Notable investments included Keyfactor's $1 billion round and Cyera's $400 million round, with both companies focusing on AI for identity and data security. M&A activity saw significant deals, such as Visa's $2.4 billion acquisition of BioCatch, emphasizing the industry's response to AI-driven security challenges.

articles.title: Rippling's Outbound GTM Strategy Is Worth $17B
articles.summary: Rippling was exhausting its account lists with automated emails before it built an outbound team in 2022. Replacing sequences with people working the same accounts reportedly lifted conversion from roughly 1% to between 3% and 7%. Reps get paid for meetings held with decision makers, and account executives don't prospect. Managers supervise just four or five reps each. Selling multiple products to each customer helps fund that staffing. Before copying the team size, calculate how much you can spend to win an account, including the additional products customers actually buy.

articles.title: Cal AI paid UFC creators thousands of dollars to post, and got no download spike at all
articles.summary: A UFC fighter needs to track calories. Someone watching the fight might have no interest in doing that. Cal AI's co-founder blames that mismatch for creator deals that cost thousands and produced no download spike. The team now reads comments for people asking for help the app provides. It caps payment per thousand views at measured revenue per thousand views, favoring flat fees to keep viral upside. One creator went from roughly 10,000 views to 7 million. Before paying for that possibility, check whether the comments contain potential customers.

articles.title: Put a name on it
articles.summary: When project updates pass through a manager, leadership can lose the details needed to unblock the work. Nordhealth puts one engineer's name on each project and has that person post a weekly update in Linear, including changed dates and a link to the work. Reading roughly 30 updates takes leadership 30 to 60 minutes, leaving four to six projects needing closer attention. The owner can book Wednesday office hours directly with leadership. Start with a blocked project and check whether its named owner can get a decision without sending the question through their manager.

articles.title: Backends on Vercel: Python, containers, and Daemons (Tool)
articles.summary: Vercel now offers generally available Python backends, containerized functions, and a public beta of Daemons for continuously running workers that pull jobs from queues or databases.

articles.title: Navige (Tool)
articles.summary: Reduce agent costs through model routing, caching, budget controls, and safeguards.

articles.title: Agent observability on the Claude Platform (Tool)
articles.summary: Claude's public beta of OpenTelemetry traces lets teams send agent turns, model calls, tool use, latency, and token usage into their existing observability tools to investigate failures and costs.

articles.title: I designed a nose guard for my dog and gave it away. Now 500 dogs wear one
articles.summary: People wanted SnoutCover's dog nose guard but couldn't easily print and assemble the free design themselves. After trying to help them find local printers, its maker opened a shop. The first order arrived 16 days after the website went up. A year later, it had 395 orders across 16 countries. Customer photos led to better straps and custom fits. The design remains free, while the shop sells finished covers. If you give away a design, check which requests are for changes to the file and which are asking you to make it.

articles.title: Abstract Warfare: How TSMC Made Its Own Market
articles.summary: TSMC made it possible to start a chip company without building a factory or depending on a manufacturer that sold competing chips. It manufactured for other designers and committed not to compete with them. A factory's huge upfront cost became something a designer could pay for as its business grew. TSMC initially survived on work existing chipmakers didn't want, while its future customers were still forming. Which expensive step must every new entrant in your market own, and could you sell that step without competing with the companies buying it?

articles.title: MIT class project turns into an FDA-cleared treatment for tremors
articles.summary: Encora's tremor wristband had people asking to buy it after a student demonstration, but it was nine years from that demonstration to FDA clearance. The MIT team chose the idea by a 16-to-one vote. Its proposer was the only dissenter. After initially working on Parkinson's, the company shifted to essential tremor, citing more patients and less drug-development activity. Its clearance covers adults with essential tremor. If your prototype attracts buyers, which patient group can you actually seek clearance to serve, and how long can you fund the trials needed to reach them?

articles.title: On the Death of Amazon's Writing Culture
articles.summary: Require human-written memos for hard-to-reverse decisions and hold presenters responsible for every sentence.

articles.title: Anthropic replaced git because git assumes a human is typing
articles.summary: Anthropic's daily merges rose from about 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September, making source control its biggest development bottleneck and leading it to build Scion, a replacement for git in its monorepo.

articles.title: The free upgrade that raised your bill
articles.summary: In a test of 191 constructed reading-assistant requests, a 33% cut in Sonnet's token prices produced a 4% higher bill with thinking off, as a changed tokenizer and longer answers increased billed tokens.

articles.title: 250 CEOs Confessed Their Pay. Half Earn Less Than Their Staff.
articles.summary: In Hampton's survey of 250 founders and CEOs, 47% paid a functional leader more than their own base salary, while none of the 58 venture-backed respondents reported more than $300,000 in compensation beyond salary.
